\chapter{Boolean Analysis — General}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Randomization.General
\section{Overview}
Randomization preserves the second norm and compares product noise with Walsh analysis on an auxiliary sign cube. Exponent-dependent noise contraction yields atom-independent bounds for low degree projection.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Pointwise randomization Parseval identity]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.randomization_pointwise_parseval}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.component, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.randomization, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.randomization_fourier_coefficient, BooleanAnalysis.expect, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.parseval}
\difficulty{1}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, and $x\in\Omega$. If $R_rf(x)=\sum_S\chi_S(r)f_S(x)$ and $r$ is uniform on the Boolean cube, then $\mathbb E_r(R_rf(x))^2=\sum_Sf_S(x)^2$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $h_S=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}E_Uh$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ (the Hoeffding--Efron--Stein components); $\chi_S(r)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{r_i}$ for $r\in\{0,1\}^n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Randomization preserves the second norm]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.randomization_norm_two}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect_sum, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.norm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.parseval, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.randomizationNorm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.randomization_pointwise_parseval}
\difficulty{3}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$ and $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. Then $(\mathbb E_{x\sim P}\mathbb E_r|\sum_S\chi_S(r)f_S(x)|^2)^{1/2}=\|f\|_{2,P}$, where $r$ is uniform on the Boolean cube. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $h_S=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}E_Uh$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ (the Hoeffding--Efron--Stein components); $\|h\|_{p,P}=(\mathbb E_P|h|^p)^{1/p}$ for $p>0$; $\chi_S(r)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{r_i}$ for $r\in\{0,1\}^n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Cube projection moment bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cube_lowDegree_projection}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.BooleanFunc, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationProjectionAux.cube_lowDegree_has_degree, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.RandomizationProjectionAux.cube_lowDegree_l2_le, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeLpNorm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cubeLpNorm_two, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.expect_rpow_abs_nonneg, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.holder_ineq_bool, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.holder_sharpness, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lowDegree_norm_ge_two, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.lp_norm_mono, BooleanAnalysis.innerProduct, BooleanAnalysis.l2Norm, BooleanAnalysis.plancherel, KKL.fourierCoeff_lowDegreePart, KKL.lowDegreePart}
\difficulty{6}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be a function on the uniform Boolean cube, $k\in\mathbb N$, and $q>1$. The Fourier projection $f^{\le k}$ satisfies $\|f^{\le k}\|_q\le(\sqrt{q-1})^k\|f\|_q$ when $q\ge2$, and $\|f^{\le k}\|_q\le(1/\sqrt{q-1})^k\|f\|_q$ when $q\le2$. For a real function $h$ on the cube, use $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{x_i}$, $\widehat h(S)=\mathbb E_x[h(x)\chi_S(x)]$, $h^{\le k}=\sum_{|S|\le k}\widehat h(S)\chi_S$, $\|h\|_p=(\mathbb E_x|h(x)|^p)^{1/p}$, with uniform expectation $\mathbb E_x$ and natural powers $0^0=1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Noisy cube projection fourth moment]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.cube_lowDegree_projection_noise}

\difficulty{5}
Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be a function on the uniform Boolean cube, $k\in\mathbb N$, and $0<\rho\le1$. Then $\|f^{\le k}\|_4\le(\sqrt3/\rho)^k\|T_\rho f\|_4$. For a real function $h$ on the cube, use $\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}(-1)^{x_i}$, $\widehat h(S)=\mathbb E_x[h(x)\chi_S(x)]$, $h^{\le k}=\sum_{|S|\le k}\widehat h(S)\chi_S$, $\|h\|_p=(\mathbb E_x|h(x)|^p)^{1/p}$, $T_a h=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}a^{|S|}\widehat h(S)\chi_S$, with uniform expectation $\mathbb E_x$ and natural powers $0^0=1$.
\end{theorem}
